clue.text: Extinct animal is around in changed form

indicators.note: something put in a changed form has had its parts rearranged, so the preceding words are shuffled

blocks.note: two words taken as written, used as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Some long-gone creature turns out to be still about, only looking different.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs are the classic example of creatures that died out entirely millions of years ago.

clue.text: Feed a mouse with cheese

indicators.note: the phrase is read as holding something within it, so the letters sit inside the words before

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Instructions for feeding a pet mouse: give it some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes cheese the food for the mouse; in fact the cheese is lurking in fEED A Mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch variety sold in round balls coated with red wax.

clue.text: Pound is good in France and capital elsewhere

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
taken as written
bon is the French word for good

explanation.surface: A remark about money: the pound does well in France, and its capital does well somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elsewhere' signals that this capital is not in France, after the French word just used: it is in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is the capital city of Portugal, a country other than the France just mentioned.

clue.text: Go on! Holiday!

blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, as in 'you're joking!'
second meaning: a short break away from home

explanation.surface: Someone urging a friend to take that holiday they keep talking about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get away!' is an exclamation of surprised disbelief, the same as 'Go on!'; a getaway is also a short break.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase serves both as an incredulous exclamation and as a noun for a brief vacation trip.

clue.text: Weigh about two pounds and a quarter, almost

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the pound abbreviation, doubled
north is one of the four compass points, a quarter in crossword terms

explanation.surface: Instructions to weigh something at around two and a quarter pounds, near enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The LL and N go inside WEIGH after its first two letters. A quarter is a compass point (N, E, S or W) in crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-nigh is a slightly old-fashioned adverb meaning very nearly or all but.

clue.text: Girl allowed by her aunt in Paris to be a dabbler

blocks.note: Di is a short girl's name
let means permitted
tante is the French word for aunt

explanation.surface: A girl's French aunt lets her try her hand at things without committing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante takes up an art or subject superficially, for amusement, never with serious study.

clue.text: They may be smoked and eaten

blocks.note: first meaning: cannabis cigarettes
second meaning: large cuts of roasted meat

explanation.surface: Something that can be both smoked and eaten, like a kipper or a ham.
explanation.walkthrough: Smoked suggests fish or bacon; instead one sense is the cannabis cigarette and the other the Sunday roast.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both rolled cannabis cigarettes and large butcher's cuts of meat for roasting.

clue.text: Blow whistle for a breathing space

blocks.note: wind is moving air, a blow
a pipe is a simple whistle-like wind instrument

explanation.surface: Someone blowing a whistle to call a pause in play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathing space' looks like a rest or pause, but here it is literally a passage that air travels through.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the tube carrying air between throat and lungs, a literal passage for respiration.

clue.text: Elite type found in newspaper production

definitions.text: Elite type found in newspaper production

blocks.clueFragment: Elite type found in newspaper production
blocks.note: surface reading: Elite is the name of a typeface, the kind of print used to set a paper
setter's reading: a top person, one of the elite, who runs a paper's output

explanation.surface: A font called Elite being used to print a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper decides its content and is senior to all its journalists.

clue.text: The hollow sound of success in business

blocks.note: first meaning: a deep resonant noise
second meaning: a period of rapid economic growth

explanation.surface: Success in business makes a hollow noise, a cynical remark about empty prosperity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a deep resonant noise and also a spell of rapid commercial growth and prosperity.

clue.text: Certainly using every available method

blocks.note: first meaning: a polite 'of course'
second meaning: read literally, through all possible ways

explanation.surface: Someone promising to try every possible approach without question.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a courteous way of granting permission, and literally describes employing every possible way.

clue.text: Be able to repeat a vigorous dance

blocks.note: can means be able
the same word said once more

explanation.surface: Being able to perform an energetic dance more than once.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a lively high-kicking chorus routine from Parisian music halls.

clue.text: One may have a fair throw at it

definitions.text: One may have a fair throw at it

blocks.clueFragment: One may have a fair throw at it
blocks.note: surface reading: a reasonable attempt or a fair chance at something
setter's reading: a throw at a fairground stall where balls are hurled to knock prizes off posts

explanation.surface: Someone getting a reasonable chance at a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fair throw' sounds like a fair go; the fair is a funfair, a travelling fairground.
explanation.definitionFit: This fairground sideshow has visitors hurling wooden balls to knock nuts from stands to win them.

clue.text: Dictates new chemistry examination involving litmus paper

indicators.note: a new version of the word is made from the same letters in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A teacher prescribes a fresh practical exam in chemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: Litmus paper turns red in acid, so the clue's definition describes the chemistry literally; the phrase also means any decisive trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a test for acidity, such as dipping blue litmus to see it turn red.

clue.text: Healthy accommodation for a prisoner charged with battery

blocks.note: first meaning: a prison room that is not damp
second meaning: a battery with a paste electrolyte rather than liquid

explanation.surface: Decent lodgings for an inmate who is accused of assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged with battery' reads as a criminal accusation, but it just links the cell definition to the electrical one.
explanation.definitionFit: This type of electric cell uses a paste electrolyte, as in an ordinary torch battery.

clue.text: Slash material price

blocks.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A shop announcing it has cut the cost of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slash' reads as a verb about cutting prices; it means cut flesh deeply.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or gash skin, as a blade or claws would.

clue.text: Risk getting left in church

definitions.note: names a place within a church; the answer is the part of the building

blocks.note: to chance something is to risk it
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone taking a gamble on being abandoned at the altar.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the area near the altar reserved for clergy and choir, a section of the building.

clue.text: Mummy's nationality

blocks.note: surface reading: the country one's mother comes from
setter's reading: an embalmed body, as in the ancient tombs by the Nile

explanation.surface: Asking where someone's mother was born.
explanation.definitionFit: Embalmed preserved bodies are most famously from the pharaohs' land along the Nile.

clue.text: They're out of step and overfussy

definitions.note: an adjective; with 'They're' it describes people, the plural noun answer

indicators.note: out of order: the words that follow are knocked out of their sequence

blocks.note: two words taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: People who march out of time are also fussy about detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of step' reads as a fixed phrase meaning nonconforming, which hides the split into indicator and letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedants are people excessively concerned with minor details and petty rules of correctness.

clue.text: Housing for a direction-finder

blocks.note: surface reading: a casing for some kind of navigation gadget
setter's reading: a ship's compass, which stands on deck in its own stand

explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the compass is mounted in a stand near the helm, so this is its case.

clue.text: Ladies in fashion becoming models

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the word is reshaped into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Women working in the fashion world end up as catwalk models.
explanation.walkthrough: The fashion picture makes models mean catwalk models; here they are perfect examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are perfect standards or exemplars worth copying, in the same sense as role models.

clue.text: It lives in Madagascar with the agreement of sailors

blocks.note: sailors acknowledge an order with a doubled old word for yes

explanation.surface: A creature living on an island, approved by passing seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: The aye-aye is a nocturnal lemur found only on that island, with a long thin middle finger.

clue.text: Business concern

blocks.note: first meaning: a matter, as in 'that is my business'
second meaning: a thing that is someone's responsibility

explanation.walkthrough: 'Business concern' reads as one phrase meaning a firm; split it, and each word separately means a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or event that someone is responsible for or involved in.

clue.text: Dutch punter gets over 50%

blocks.note: a punter is someone who places bets
fifty per cent is one half

explanation.surface: A gambler from Holland lands odds of better than evens.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is not about Holland: 'my old Dutch' is London slang for one's wife, from rhyming slang duchess of Fife.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are affectionate, jokey British terms for a man's wife or spouse.

clue.text: Small amounts put on horses

blocks.note: first meaning: little pieces
second meaning: metal mouthpieces fitted on a horse's bridle

explanation.surface: Modest stakes placed on a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on horses' suggests betting small amounts; instead it is tack placed in the horse's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means small pieces, and also metal bars fixed in a horse's mouth for steering.

clue.text: Harbour transport

blocks.note: first meaning: to hold within
second meaning: to carry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbour transport' suggests ferries in a port; both words are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear means to nurse a feeling such as a grudge, and also to carry something along.

clue.text: Out-of-date, like a tricorn for example

definitions.note: the second sense is a noun phrase, an aged piece of headwear

blocks.note: first meaning: unfashionable, stale
second meaning, read literally: a piece of headwear from long ago

explanation.walkthrough: A tricorn is the three-cornered hat of the 18th century, literally an ancient piece of headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes stale, hackneyed ideas, and literally it is an aged item of headwear.

clue.text: Vessel manoeuvring in River Tamar

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving about, so the letters are moved into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the map abbreviation for river
taken as written; the Tamar divides Devon from Cornwall

explanation.surface: A boat steering its way along a river in the West of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a sailing boat with three parallel hulls, a type of seagoing craft.
